newsitem.title: UK: Most Britons unimpressed by budget - poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Britons unimpressed by budget - poll.

text.p: Britons were generally unimpressed by Tuesday's budget from Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke, with only 17 percent believing it would make them better off, according to an opinion poll published on Wednesday.
Clarke, the chancellor of the exchequer, announced the basic rate of income tax would fall one point to 23 percent. He also raised taxes on petrol, cigarettes and air travel.
The NOP poll, published in the Evening Standard newspaper, said about eight of 10 Britons thought the budget would leave them worse off or make no difference.
Almost half said they believed the Conservatives would raise the basic rate of tax again if they won the next election, which must be held by May 1997.

Only 20 percent believed the budget was fair for the country as a whole. Twenty seven percent of those polled believed Clarke when he said the economy was prosperous and successful, but 61 percent disagreed.
NOP polled 545 adults by telephone on Tuesday.
